properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1 in the shipped libsignal crypto layer: CryptographicHash dispatches by algorithm name ("SHA-1"/"SHA1") to a real Sha1 implementation (rust/crypto/src/hash.rs), and zkgroup derives user IDs via a UUIDv5-style SHA-1 (uid_struct.rs:91). Purpose: legacy/compat hashing and name-based identifier derivation, not collision-resistance-dependent security. Weak-hash exposure is real and changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-256-CBC as implemented in signal_crypto (rust/crypto/src/aes_cbc.rs) and consumed by the group cipher, legacy session cipher, triple-ratchet message layer, username links, and message-backup frames. Keys/IVs come from HKDF-derived message keys and messages are MACed with HMAC-SHA256 by the calling protocol layer, so the CBC use is authenticated end-to-end; the aes_cbc.rs test block covers the KATs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-256-CTR paired with HMAC-SHA256 (Encrypt-then-MAC) in two production paths: the session/triple-ratchet message cipher (rust/protocol/src/crypto.rs aes_256_ctr_encrypt/decrypt + hmac_sha256) and SVR-B backup metadata encryption (rust/net/src/svrb.rs aes_256_ctr_encrypt_hmacsha256 with a random 12-byte IV). CTR is authenticated by the attached HMAC at the protocol layer, so the classic unauthenticated-CTR concern does not apply; remaining sites are unit tests of the same functions.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA-1 exposed by the shipped crypto layer: rust/crypto CryptographicMac accepts "HMACSha1" (enum HmacSha1 over sha1), mirrored by the JCE-compat wrapper java Mac.java:23 and exercised by CryptographicMacTests KATs. No production caller found in this tree — a legacy/compat MAC surface shipped in the library.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Non-cryptographic PRNGs used exclusively in test code: java.util.Random in Java unit tests (GroupCipherTest, PQXDHBundleFactory, SessionBuilderTest) and Math.random() for shuffling test vectors in node/ts/test/util.ts. No production key material derives from these.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Poly1305 appears only as the authentication tag inside the ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD: the chacha20poly1305 crate declarations and the snow_resolver's ChaCha20Poly1305 encrypt/decrypt-with-detached-tag calls (rust/attest). Same logical asset as the ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD object.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 is the classical half of Signal's hybrid key agreement: PQXDH combines X25519 ECDH with Kyber-1024 for prekey exchange, the Double Ratchet steps are X25519 ECDH, identity keys double as X25519 keys via the XEdDSA-style construction, and curve25519-dalek 5.0 provides the implementation. Harvest-now-decrypt-later for all recorded traffic; migration ML-KEM-768 hybrid — already partially deployed via PQXDH (Kyber) and the spqr post-quantum ratchet.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 is Signal's identity-key signature scheme: device identity keys, signed prekeys, and server certificate chains are Ed25519 (ed25519-dalek 3.0); the ed_to_xed.rs example demonstrates the Ed25519↔X25519 mapping behind Signal's use of one key pair for both signing and DH. Quantum-vulnerable signatures protecting the whole trust model; migration ML-DSA-65/SLH-DSA per Signal's PQ roadmap (PQXDH/SPQR already cover the KEX half). Quantum-vulnerable; curve fixed by Intel's DCAP format (observable, replaceable only upstream).

Quantum-vulnerable signature verification of enclave attestations, but the algorithm is fixed by Intel's DCAP specification (observable here, replaceable only upstream); migration ML-DSA when the ecosystem moves.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-256-GCM AEAD throughout the client stack: Java Aes256GcmEncryption/Decryption JNI wrappers, Rust protocol/zkgroup/net call sites, and native equivalents — the primary authenticated cipher for sealed sender v2, zkgroup blobs, and network frames. Symmetric AEAD (Grover-reduced margin only, no Shor exposure); strong as configured. Note: name-similarity regexes may have folded AES-GCM-SIV sites into this object; GCM-SIV is reported separately where distinct.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Kyber (Kyber-1024 and Kyber-768 parameter sets) is the post-quantum half of Signal's PQXDH hybrid prekey exchange (X25519+Kyber1024), implemented via the KEM abstraction in rust/protocol/src/kem.rs and exercised in benchmarks/tests/fuzz targets. Already post-quantum-secure; the NIST-standardized successor is ML-KEM, which is also present (ALG-990f5513) for the next protocol generation.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA-256 is the protocol workhorse MAC: message authentication in the session cipher (Encrypt-then-MAC with AES-CTR/CBC), SVR backup metadata, CDSI, and the JCE-compat Mac wrapper (Mac.java accepts "HMACSha256"). Strong, not quantum-broken (Groner-reduced security only).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 across the stack: HKDF/HMAC underpinnings, certificate and digest uses, and build/archive tooling (bin/fetch_archive.py, node/build_node_bridge.py checksum archives). Standard digest, no weakness.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ML-KEM (FIPS 203) present as the standardized successor to Kyber: declared via the ml-kem crate (Cargo.toml:160) and selectable in the protocol KEM layer (KeyType::MLKEM1024 in rust/protocol/src/kem.rs) for next-generation PQXDH variants. Post-quantum-secure by design.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HKDF (SHA-256 based) is the key-derivation layer everywhere: message keys from chain keys, sealed sender v2 keys (Hkdf<sha2::Sha256> at sealed_sender.rs:1049), backup/SVR key derivation, account keys. Standard, PQ-relevant only via its hash (SHA-256, fine).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Argon2id for account key derivation from the account entropy pool / PIN-adjacent material in rust/account-keys and declared via the argon2 crate. Memory-hard KDF; strong, not quantum-broken.
